summary.title: Rebuilding Git in Ruby
summary.one_liner: You learn how Git's core internals work by re-implementing its init, add, and commit commands as a small Ruby tool called RGit.
keywords: how does git work under the hood
git head and refs heads master
takeaways: Git's top-level command proxies to separate subcommand scripts, following the UNIX convention of small tools.
Running init creates a .git directory with HEAD, config, objects, and refs subdirectories; HEAD holds a ref to the master branch.
git add hashes file contents with SHA1, stores a zlib-compressed blob in objects/, and records the SHA and path in the index.
git commit builds nested tree objects from the index, creates a commit object pointing at the root tree, and updates the current branch ref.
The object graph (commit to tree to blob) is what lets Git move between points in history by changing pointers.
summary.summary: The article walks through re-implementing a simplified Git, called RGit, in Ruby. It covers a top-level rgit dispatcher script, then rgit-init to create the .rgit directory layout and HEAD file, and rgit-add to hash, compress, and store file contents as blobs while writing an index. It finishes with rgit-commit, which builds tree objects from the index, writes a commit object, updates the branch ref, and clears the index. The author uses a simplified text index instead of Git's binary format for clarity.
